Neha / Marissa — draft numbers below (sending as internal note; I will attach a formatted ratecard sheet for procurement). Open to adjustments based on exact QPS and SLA needs.

Pricing model (hosted API, per-eval billing):
- Classifier endpoint (per-candidate score): $0.012 per 1,000 candidate-scores (i.e., $0.000012 per candidate-score).
- Reranker endpoint (neural rerank scoring): $0.035 per 1,000 candidate-scores (i.e., $0.000035 per candidate-score).
- Request/overhead fee: $0.002 per 1,000 requests to cover routing/metrics (~$0.000002 per request).

Batch behavior: for batched calls (one request with N candidates), we bill per candidate-score. Multiple scoring passes are additive — every model forward that scores a candidate counts as a candidate-score. Token-level caching helps reduce model tokenization cost but does not remove the neural scoring charge.

Example: 1,000,000 queries x 10 candidates = 10,000,000 candidate-scores
- Classifier-only path (if you only call classifier): 10,000,000 * $0.000012 = $120.
- Reranker for top-10 (neural rerank score for all 10): 10,000,000 * $0.000035 = $350.
- Request overhead: 1,000,000 * $0.000002 = $2.
- Total (rerank path): ~$352 / month (hosted, pay-as-you-go) — note this is unit-only and excludes any optional observability add-ons or storage.

Discounting / commitments:
- Volume tiers: >5M candidate-scores/month: 10% discount; >15M/month: 15% discount.
- 12-month commitment: additional 8% off unit pricing (stackable with volume tiers).
- POC Eval credits: we can provide up to 200k candidate-score credits for a 30-day POC.

Alternative: Dedicated slot pricing for predictable latency and cost: fixed monthly commit for a dedicated pool — we can run numbers if they prefer an S-level commitment.

Attaching a proposed ratecard (Proposed_Ratecard_v3.xlsx) and a sample invoice for 1.25M queries so procurement can see line-item breakout.

-Marcus

Hi Olivia / procurement — thanks for the questions, answering inline below and attaching the sample invoice and final ratecard.

1) Multi-stage scoring: our billing is per neural scoring operation. If you run a cheap classifier first and only rerank top-K, you only pay the neural reranker charge for those candidates that are actually scored by the reranker. The classifier (if it’s a model call) is billed as a classifier candidate-score if it uses a model forward. In short: we count each model forward that produces a score. If your pipeline is classifier-only for 90% of candidates and rerank-only for the top-K, the math follows exactly per-candidate counts.

2) Billing by unique candidate: we don’t currently support collapsing charges automatically by "unique id" at invoice-time because billing is usage-driven and tied to model forward events. If you can dedupe upstream and avoid making the scoring call, you will not be billed. We can explore custom invoicing for large enterprise customers as part of a Dedicated/contract discussion.

3) Caching: token-level and prefix caching reduce model tokenization and can materially reduce infra cost, but they do not change how many neural forward ops are billed if the model still executes to score the candidate. Caching benefits are most visible when you reuse candidate representations across queries (e.g., embedding + lookup) — in those cases you can avoid model forwards entirely. We’ll include notes in the ratecard on how caching patterns interact with billed units.

4) Sample invoice: attached "Sample_Invoice_1.25M_queries.xlsx" — line items include classifier candidate-scores, reranker candidate-scores, request overhead, and applied tier/commit discounts.

Next steps:
- I propose a 30-min alignment call with Olivia, Daniel (procurement), their infra SRE, Marcus, and me next Tue/Wed. Please reply with a couple of preferred windows and we’ll lock in.
- We’ll provision 200k eval candidate-score credits for Shoplytics POC (30 days) once NDA procurement path is agreed.

Thanks — attaching final ratecard and sample invoice.
